correctness.rationale: The RKHS norm yields the cellwise Euler–Lagrange equation and unique explicit spline interpolant. Integrating produces a common positive gamma-dependent correction to nonnegative hat moments. A circle-convolution rearrangement proves the minimum hat moment is P_N at a sine-density zero. Orthogonal Fourier series give exact even/odd H_N. Their strict inequalities and monotone correction yield a unique sharp crossing and all equality cases. The Taylor/cotangent expansion yields the stated two-term law. Standalone tests independently rebuild Gram systems and compare exact formulas for 2<=N<=14; finite tests are corroboration, not the universal proof.

The 2026 source provides the method but not this exact sign classification. General representer theorems and convergence guarantees do not imply the sharp threshold without the new extremal analysis. Historical-priority uncertainty remains, especially older periodic Sobolev spline work.

value.rationale: A direct mathematical/stability gap exists: the new sine-periodized kernel quadrature determines optimized signed weights without a criterion for nonnegative integration of positive data. The exact gamma_N classifies all finite grid sizes and all kernel parameters, identifies a genuine sign transition, and quantifies a nontrivial linear-in-grid threshold with explicit second term. It supplies an interpretable parameter-design benchmark not supplied by asymptotic error bounds; no general multidimensional positivity claim is inferred.
